The Tulsa County Courthouse stands as a symbol of justice, history, and architectural brilliance in the heart of Tulsa, Oklahoma. This iconic landmark has played a pivotal role in the city's development, serving as the center of legal activities and providing essential services to the community. With its rich history, distinctive architecture, and important functions, the Tulsa County Courthouse continues to be a significant institution in the region.

Tulsa County Courthouse location

The Tulsa County Courthouse, located at500 S Denver Ave., Tulsa, OK 74103, USA, is a magnificent building that has been an integral part of Tulsa's landscape since its completion in 1953 . Its imposing presence and architectural grandeur make it a recognizable landmark in the city. As the seat of justice for Tulsa County, the courthouse serves as the administrative hub for various legal processes, including trials, hearings, and record-keeping.

Historical Significance of the Courthouse

The history of the Tulsa County Courthouse is deeply intertwined with the growth and development of the city. The original courthouse, constructed in 1912, was a modest building that couldn't accommodate the increasing demands of the expanding community. As Tulsa flourished, it became necessary to construct a larger and more modern courthouse to meet the evolving needs.

The current courthouse, a magnificent example of Classical Revival, was completed in 1912. Its historical significance lies in its association with several notable events in Tulsa's past.Over the years, it has witnessed countless trials, making it an essential part of Tulsa's legal history.

Tulsa Municipal Court

The Tulsa Municipal Court is the judicial branch of the City of Tulsa government and handles cases involving violations of city ordinances. The court has jurisdiction over traffic violations, misdemeanors, municipal code violations, and some small claims cases within the Tulsa city limits. The purpose of municipal court is to provide fair, impartial, and accessible administration of justice while upholding legal rights and resolving legal matters in an efficient manner.

Jurisdiction and Powers

The Tulsa Municipal Court has jurisdiction over Class A and B misdemeanors committed within Tulsa city limits. This includes both criminal and traffic misdemeanor cases punishable by fines and jail time of up to 6 months. The court also handles city ordinance violations and some small claims civil cases up to $7,500.

Municipal judges are granted considerable power to set bonds, issue warrants, subpoena witnesses, punish contempt of court, and impose penalties if a defendant is found or pleads guilty. However, the court does not conduct jury trials.

Types of Cases

Some of the most common types of cases handled by the Tulsa Municipal Court include:

  • Traffic violations – speeding, stop sign/light violations, seat belt tickets, driving without insurance, etc.
  • Misdemeanor assault and battery charges
  • Petty theft and shoplifting
  • Public intoxication and drunk and disorderly conduct
  • Vandalism and graffiti
  • Housing code violations
  • Noise complaints and nuisance abatement issues

Court Organization and Staff

The Tulsa Municipal Court is overseen by the Presiding Municipal Judge and the Court Administrator. The court staff is comprised of judges, prosecutors, clerks, and other support personnel across its various divisions.

Judges

Tulsa Municipal Court currently has 5 municipal judges who preside over arraignments, trials, and other court proceedings. The judges are appointed by the Mayor and confirmed by the City Council.

Judge Douglas Golden

Judge Douglas Golden serves as the Presiding Municipal Judge and oversees administration of the court. He was appointed to the bench in 2019 after previously serving as a prosecutor. Judge Golden earned his law degree from the University of Tulsa.

Court Administrator

The Court Administrator manages court staff and operations and makes recommendations on policy and procedural changes. The current Court Administrator is Susan Witt.

City Prosecutors

The Tulsa City Prosecutor's Office handles misdemeanor cases before the court with a staff of assistant city prosecutors. The Prosecutor's Office is under the direction of the elected City Attorney.

Court Process and Procedures

The Tulsa Municipal Court handles a high volume of cases annually. The court process begins when a citation or violation notice is issued by law enforcement or city code enforcement officers.

Filing a Case

Traffic Cases

For traffic violations, the ticket serves as the formal charge and is filed with the court. Motorists are given a date to appear for arraignment.

Criminal Cases

Misdemeanor criminal cases begin when the prosecutor's office files a complaint or citation after review of a police report. A warrant for the defendant's arrest may be issued.

Arraignments and Trials

Options for Traffic Cases

For traffic arraignments, motorists can plead guilty or no contest and pay the fine, request a hearing to contest the ticket, or request a deferred disposition.

Criminal Trials

Misdemeanor criminal cases involve formal arraignments and trials before a judge if defendants plead not guilty. Prosecutors have burden of proving guilt beyond a reasonable doubt.

Paying Fines and Fees

Fines, court costs, and fees are due at time of sentencing or adjudication for both traffic and criminal cases. The court accepts various payment methods.

Payment Methods

The Municipal Court accepts payments online, by phone, mail, or in person. Cash, checks, money orders and credit/debit cards are accepted. Time payments plans may also be arranged.

Contesting Payments

Defendants believing they were wrongly charged fines or fees can file a claim of excessive costs and request a hearing before a judge.

Court Records and Information

Court records are maintained by the Municipal Court Clerk's office and are considered public records in most cases.

Obtaining Court Records

To obtain municipal court records, members of the public can visit the courthouse in person or request records by email, phone, or mail. Fees may apply for copies.

Court Website and Online Services

The Municipal Court website provides information on divisions, dockets, judges, payments, and other services. The public can search case records, pay fines, and request records online.

Tulsa County Court Clerk

The Tulsa County Court Clerk's office serves as the administrative hub for court-related activities in the county. It handles a wide range of responsibilities, including maintaining court records, processing legal documents, and providing assistance to attorneys, litigants, and the general public. The court clerk's office plays a crucial role in ensuring transparency, accessibility, and efficiency within the judicial system.

Accessing Tulsa County Court Records Online

In today's digital age, accessing court records online has become increasingly convenient. The Tulsa County Court Clerk's office offers an online portal that allows individuals to search for and access court records from the comfort of their homes or offices. By visiting the official website of the Tulsa County Court Clerk, users can navigate the online system and retrieve the desired court records by providing relevant search criteria, such as case number, party names, or date of filing.

Exploring Free Tulsa County Court Records

For those seeking free access to Tulsa County court records, the Court Clerk's office provides public access terminals within its premises. These terminals allow individuals to search for and view court records without incurring any charges. By using the public access terminals, visitors can retrieve information about specific cases, review court filings, and obtain copies of documents, all at no cost.

Conducting a Tulsa County Records Search

The Tulsa County Court Clerk's office is also a valuable resource for conducting comprehensive records searches. Whether it's a criminal case, a civil lawsuit, a probate matter, or any other legal proceeding, individuals can visit the Court Clerk's office and request assistance in locating specific records. Trained staff members are available to guide visitors through the search process, ensuring that relevant records are located efficiently.

The Role of Tulsa County District Court

The Tulsa County District Court is an essential component of the local judicial system. It serves as the venue for a wide range of legal proceedings, including criminal trials, civil lawsuits, family law matters, and probate cases. The District Court operates within the Tulsa County Courthouse and works in conjunction with the Court Clerk's office to provide seamless judicial services.

Contacting the Tulsa County Court Clerk by Phone

If individuals have inquiries or require assistance regarding court-related matters, they can reach out to the Tulsa County Court Clerk's office by phone. The Court Clerk's office provides a dedicated phone number that allows individuals to speak with knowledgeable staff members who can provide guidance, answer questions, and offer support with various court-related inquiries.

Case Search at the Tulsa County Courthouse

For those preferring an in-person approach to accessing court information, the Tulsa County Courthouse offers a case search service. Visitors can visit the courthouse and approach the designated information desk, where courthouse staff will assist in searching for and retrieving specific case details. This service enables individuals to obtain accurate and up-to-date information directly from the courthouse's records.

Contact Information for the Tulsa County Courthouse

If individuals need to contact the Tulsa County Courthouse for any reason, such as scheduling a hearing, obtaining information about court proceedings, or addressing administrative matters, the courthouse provides a dedicated phone number. By calling this phone number, individuals can connect with the appropriate courthouse departments or personnel who can address their specific needs.

Accessing Docket Information at the Tulsa County Courthouse

The Tulsa County Courthouse maintains comprehensive docket information, which provides a schedule of upcoming court hearings, trials, and other legal proceedings. Visitors can access docket information either online through the Court Clerk's website or by visiting the courthouse in person. Docket information ensures that interested parties can stay informed about court activities and plan their attendance accordingly.

Obtaining Tulsa County Divorce Records

For individuals seeking Tulsa County divorce records, the Court Clerk's office is the primary resource. By submitting a request to the Court Clerk's office, individuals can obtain certified copies of divorce decrees, marriage dissolution documents, and related records. The Court Clerk's office follows a specific process for requesting and obtaining divorce records, ensuring the privacy and security of sensitive information.

FAQs

1. Can I visit the Tulsa County Courthouse?

Absolutely! The Tulsa County Courthouse welcomes visitors and offers guided tours to explore its historical and architectural wonders.

Q: What are the standard business hours for Tulsa Municipal Court?

A: The court is open Monday through Friday from 8am to 5pm, except on city-observed holidays.

Q: Does Tulsa Municipal Court handle felony cases?

A: No, felony criminal cases are under the jurisdiction of the Tulsa County District Court.

Q: Can I have a case transferred from Municipal Court to a different court?

A: No, cases cannot be transferred as the Municipal Court has exclusive jurisdiction over city ordinance violations committed within Tulsa.

Q: Is there a dress code for appearing in Municipal Court? A: Yes, proper attire such as business casual is required when appearing before a judge. Hats, shorts, and flip flops are prohibited.
